description: The science of how speech works — the theory the agent can hold its OWN speech system up against. Three pillars: PRODUCTION (how a speaker turns intention into an acoustic signal), PERCEPTION (how a listener turns the signal back into linguistic units), and ACQUISITION (how an infant learns both via the sensorimotor babble loop). Each pillar is decomposed into its sub-mechanisms by an expansion pack in seeds/expansions/. This Mt is the theoretical map; the agent's phonology Mt + pipeline + cortices are the implementation it assesses against this map.

concepts.name: speech_production
concepts.definition: How a speaker turns a communicative intention into a radiated acoustic signal: the articulatory chain of respiration (airflow), phonation (vocal-fold vibration giving voicing + pitch), and articulation (the vocal tract shaped by place/manner of articulation), understood through source-filter theory and shaped by coarticulation and prosody.

concepts.name: speech_perception
concepts.definition: How a listener recovers linguistic units from the acoustic signal: peripheral auditory analysis, mapping continuous acoustics to discrete categories (categorical perception) via acoustic cues, solving the lack-of-invariance and segmentation problems, normalising for speaker/rate, and accessing the lexicon.

concepts.name: speech_acquisition
concepts.definition: How an infant comes to produce AND perceive its native language: the sensorimotor babble loop that grounds the perception-production mapping by hearing one's own output, plus perceptual narrowing from a universal to a native listener, statistical learning of the sound inventory, and the vocabulary explosion that follows category stabilisation.

wiring_note: Speech_science is wired UP into the substrate's four foundational pillars of speech as a phenomenon. linguistics_foundation: the broader linguistic field speech encodes. audio_psychoacoustics: the perception layer through which speech enters. embodied_motor: the motor production layer (articulator control). cybernetics_systems: the closed-loop feedback under which speech is produced and perceived (DAF effect, motor theory of speech perception, articulatory feedback loops). Together: speech is linguistic content perceived through audition, produced by motor + regulated by cybernetic feedback.
